title: Exact Maximin Allocation for Three-Arm Ordered Binary Trials with Conditional Likelihood-Ratio Tests
banked_reason: D0.5 graded incremental below the field floor: the advertised general allocation and least-favorable phase remains open after five D0 solve rounds.
gap_reasons: The advertised general exact allocation/least-favorable phase characterization remains explicitly open; the delivered N=4 phase and thin-endpoint family are a materially weaker kernel, so the flagship positioning must be reduced or the general phase object supplied.

The advertised missing object—finite-sample maximin allocation for general N—remains open: the note completely solves only N=4 and characterizes least-favorable curves only for the special family (1,m,1) under a restrictive level range.
proof_attempt_summary: Five D0 solve rounds established exact conditional calibration, ordered unbiasedness, a complete N=4 allocation phase, and a least-favorable characterization for the (1,m,1) family. The promised general-N allocation phase and the prespecified N<=20 exact phase classification remain open; D0.5 graded the delivered package incremental, below the field floor. A later run can reuse the specialized proofs but must supply a structural general-N theorem or full finite phase certificates.
tldr: The project studies exact finite-sample maximin positive integer allocation for a three-arm ordered binary experiment analyzed by a conditionally calibrated order-restricted likelihood-ratio test. Boundary randomization has exact conditional size and is conditionally unbiased in every total-success stratum. The one-success stratum now gives the explicit certificate \(B_n^{\mathrm R}(p)-\alpha\ge (n_1n_3/N)\prod_j(1-p_j)^{n_j}\{p_3/(1-p_3)-p_1/(1-p_1)\}\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\). Hence every allocation obeys \(V_n^{\mathrm R}\ge\alpha+C_N\) and \(VNR\ge\alpha+C_N\), where \(C_N=\delta(\epsilon+\delta)\epsilon^{N-1}\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}/[N(1-\epsilon)(1-\epsilon-\delta)]>0\). This finite-sample margin does not imply monotonicity in endpoint separation. Exact gap reduction is proved for all positive allocations at total size four when \(0<\alpha\leq1/6\) and for every thin-endpoint allocation in its stated level range. At \(N=4\), the complete allocation phase has the closed-form maximin value \(VNR=\alpha[1+\delta\{1+(\epsilon+\delta)+(\epsilon+\delta)^2\}]\). The infinite thin-endpoint least-favorable family, reflection, and a conservative-calibration budget reversal complete the certified base; uniform gap reduction and the general allocation phase remain open.
gap: Gaussian ordered-treatment theory gives endpoint-only approximate maximin designs, while exact ordered-binomial work calibrates tests and evaluates power at fixed allocations. Positive integer allocation changes the conditional sample space and the randomized cutoff in every total-success stratum, so neither literature determines the exact robust allocation.
fill: The project derives exact power polynomials and least-favorable branches, proves gap and reflection reductions, and uses pooled boundary submodels with Bernstein sign certificates to characterize \(\Gamma_N\) or its explicit failure cells.
